page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on KVM virtualization and powered by the AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with symmetric multithreading at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. It includes 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per virtual core. It does not include bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block storage and CPU execution for all compute routines. System networking offers a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong raw processor performance and multithreaded capacity. The instance achieves top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core (2696.28) and multi-core (86177.99) evaluations, as well as an aggregate PassMark CPU score of 59279.8. Multi-threaded compilation tasks, such as compiling software with Clang, register in the top 25 percent alongside PassMark database operations and cryptographic tests. In contrast, general memory-intensive throughput over large blocks falls into average percentiles, with 85.17 GB/sec read and 38.01 GB/sec write bandwidth, alongside average Redis SET throughput and standard static web serving numbers.

Without local NVMe drives, I/O performance is bound to network storage limits, and workloads requiring low-latency scratch disks must account for this constraint. Given its balanced resource ratios and robust CPU throughput, the instance delivers high resource density and operational cost efficiency for scale-out backends. Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.16xlarge is well positioned for enterprise web applications, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed database engines, small-model LLM inference, and large-scale ETL processing jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose KVM cloud instance configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz, paired with 256 GB of RAM. Conforming to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the server omits local storage and discrete GPUs, routing all storage operations over the network and offering a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-quartile performance in multithreaded stress testing, Clang software builds, cryptographic tasks, and database routines, while general-purpose large-block memory bandwidth and Redis operations remain in average percentiles. Balancing high compute density with extensive memory capacity, this instance fits enterprise backend services, distributed databases, large-scale continuous integration compilation pipelines, and lightweight machine learning inference workloads.
